title: Aurora rollout bridge & backfill cheatsheet
content:
Summary:
A compact day-of playpad for the ‘Aurora’ feature rollout designed to bridge traffic lanes, perform backfill for cached prefixes, and provide immediate remediation steps for in-flight regressions. This is intentionally terse (field notes style) — use the full confluence plan for long-form references.

Scope:
- Services: inference-gateway, routing-proxy, cache-layer, telemetry-collector
- Regions: us-west-2 (primary), eu-central-1 (mirror), ap-southeast-1 (smoke only)
- Constraints: Dedicated pool autoscale disabled for first 60m to keep stable capacity profile

TL;DR rollout windows (PDT):
- 08:00 — Preflight / dry run (synth traffic + smoke)
- 09:00 — Canary lane 1 (1% global) — 20m observation
- 09:30 — Canary lane 2 (5% global) — 30m observation + verify latency P50/P95
- 10:30 — Gradual ramp (5 -> 25 -> 50) over 90m with pauses at 25 and 50%
- 12:30 — Full traffic if all gates green; else hold and triage

Day-of checklist (quick toggles):
- [ ] Confirm ownership roster for release window (pager/SLACK-DM list)
- [ ] Lock autoscale: set min=max to avoid noisy capacity changes
- [ ] Ensure canary routing policy points to model:v2 and compatible quantized variant
- [ ] Warm KV cache: run prefix-warm job (job id: ROLL-WARM-2147)
- [ ] Run smoke suite: generation-smoke, streaming-smoke, embedding-sanity (see runbook commands)
- [ ] Snapshot baseline telemetry: token cost, p50/p95 latency, error-rate (last 24h)
- [ ] Notify customer-success and runway on Slack channel #release-aurora

Observability smoke tests (explicit checks):
- Test 1: simple prompt roundtrip < 1200ms p95 for us-west-2
- Test 2: large context (6k tokens) memory+kv sanity — no OOMs in serving-runtime logs
- Test 3: embedding consistency sample (3 queries) — cosine delta < 0.02 vs baseline
- Test 4: telemetry sampling ensures token-level billing emitted with route metadata

Traffic ramp & throttle curve (recommended):
- 1% for 20m -> evaluate errors and latency delta
- 5% for 30m -> run automated eval set (eval-suite/aurora-quick)
- 25% pause 30m -> confirm economic signal (tokens/sec cost bump <= 8%)
- 50% pause 45m -> sample logs for KV hit-rate and tail latency
- 100% -> 60m guard window with higher sampling and alert sensitivity
Notes: keep a conservative exponential backoff for each stage if p95 > baseline*1.3 or error-rate > 0.5%

Rollback triggers (hard and soft):
- Hard triggers (immediate rollback): sustained 5xx spike > 1% requests for > 5m, OOMs in runtime, customer-facing errors (>= 3 P1 reports in 30m)
- Soft triggers (hold & triage): p95 > baseline*1.3, token-cost > baseline*1.2, KV miss-rate increase > 15%
Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Flip routing policy to fallback-model:stable (api call: /admin/routing/flip?policy=aurora), announce to PTL
2) Scale dedicated pool to previous committed image if needed
3) Trigger alert channel and rotate incident lead every 30m until stable

Backfill & cache warming strategy (field notes):
- Kick off parallel warm jobs targeting top 500 prefixes by qps; stream warm results to /tmp/backfill-report.json
- If prefix warm fails for >10% keys, defer ramp by one stage and increase KV cache TTL temporarily
- Post-ramp, run low-priority backfill to reach steady-state cache hit-rate by 24h

Communications runbook (who says what):
- Slack #release-aurora: minute-by-minute short updates from release conductor (format: STATUS | PCT | NOTE)
- Email to execs if ramp > 50% or any P1 incident triggered
- Customer success: proactive note to top-10 customers at 50% ramp with known risk items

Post-release notes template (fill quickly after go-live):
- What: Aurora model rollout (v2) — update to attention kernel + quantized path
- Who: Release lead: Maya Chen; Oncall: Marcus Lee; SRE: Eliot Gomez
- When: 2027-04-12 10:30 PDT (full traffic)
- Observed: p50/p95, error-rate, kv-hit-rate, token cost delta (insert snapshot values)
- Follow-ups: backfill progress, perf tuning (kernels A/B), sticky regressions (if any)

Open questions / TODOs (quick capture):
- Q: Should we enable burst pool for ap-southeast-1 smoke after 25%? (Priya to decide)
- TODO: Add automated rollback hook to routing service (ticket ROLL-2201)
- TODO: Update release checklist to include quantization-check per-model variant

Appendix: run commands & quick links
- Warm job: infra/scripts/warm_prefixes.sh --job ROLL-WARM-2147
- Smoke suite: tools/smoke/run_smoke.sh --suite aurora-compact
- Quick dashboards: https://console.redwood.com/d/aurora/rollout, sampling views on telemetry-collector
- Incident channel: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CRELEASEAURORA

Notes to self: keep this as the day-of quick playpad. If anything unexpected, call for canary freeze and escalate to platform-eng lead.
